issues.claim: The article on Martin Fowler's site describes strong-style pairing, where an idea reaches the code only through the partner's hands; with a large experience gap this makes the mentor explain and the learner understand.
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt does not mention strong-style pairing or the 'idea must go through someone else's hands' wording. It only shows advice that the more experienced person should sit in the navigator's seat and give the driver space. The generator itself says the large-experience-gap claim is from memory. I cannot confirm from the excerpt that the article ties strong-style pairing to a large experience gap. The same applies to locales.ru.explanation.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the full article text. If strong-style is covered there, keep the claim. Otherwise rewrite it to what the excerpt shows: 'the more experienced person should mostly navigate and give the driver space to figure things out', and drop the strong-style attribution. Make the same change in ru.

issues.claim: Pair programming is one of the fastest ways to transfer knowledge.
issues.problem: This is stated as fact but is not supported by the cited article excerpt, which stresses that pairing has many challenges. It is not attributed to any source, so it reads as unsupported opinion.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it: 'Pairing is an effective way to transfer knowledge on hard parts', or move it into the sentence about the article only if the article supports it. Update ru to match.

issues.claim: Кто в итоге должен понимать изменение и уметь сделать следующее такое же сам?
issues.problem: The hint reveals the central idea (the author must understand and own the change). It is acceptable as a nudge, but it is close to the answerHinge.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally make it vaguer, e.g. 'Чему научится junior, если готовый код просто появится в его ветке?' Apply the same to en.

issues.claim: The Google SRE book gives this as the main reason to keep postmortems blameless and to focus them on contributing causes and owned follow-up actions.
issues.problem: The chapter warns that a blame culture makes people hide issues for fear of punishment, but it does not call this 'the main reason'. The excerpt does not show that passage at all. The attribution overstates the source. The same applies to locales.ru.explanation ('главной причиной').
issues.suggestedFix: Rewrite: 'The Google SRE book warns that in a culture of finger-pointing people will not bring issues to light for fear of punishment, which is why it treats blamelessness as a core tenet and focuses postmortems on contributing causes and owned follow-up actions.' Make the same change in ru.

issues.claim: Deliberate sabotage is a different situation and is handled separately, not through the postmortem.
issues.problem: This is reasonable just-culture practice but is not in the cited sources. The text reads as if it were part of the source's position.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep it, but phrase it as general practice: 'In practice, deliberate sabotage is a separate matter outside the postmortem', so it is not read as coming from the SRE book. Do the same in ru.
